Condition-controlled while loops

Unit 1 · Week 4 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Python editor, paper trace grids and a known school-editor Stop command. Discuss non-termination on paper before running.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Condition-controlled while loops

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Success means trace a pre-test while loop, identify initialisation and update, and explain how the condition becomes False. Begin with a small bounded counter so learners can compare with for.

2. Retrieval: the range boundary

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and paired explanation

Expected range(1,4) produces 1,2,3 and excludes 4. A final print outside the loop runs once. Initialising a total inside the loop discards earlier accumulated values. Ask learners to retrieve before notes, then correct their explanation.

3. A condition checked before every pass

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher modelling and guided prediction

Trace count=1, condition True, print 1, update to 2. Continue through 3 then update to 4. At 4 the condition is False, so the body stops and Finished prints. Output 1,2,3,Finished on separate lines. Check the condition before entry and after each update. Ask a learner to narrate the last failed check.

4. The final check belongs in the trace

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked trace with faded support

Model the first two rows, then learners complete rows for count 3 and 4. At 3, True prints 3 and updates to 4. At 4, False prints nothing inside the body and performs no update. Support: keep condition column headings. Stretch: explain why there are four condition checks but only three body executions.

5. A while loop may run zero times

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided variation and peer explanation

Change the start value to 4. The first condition is False, so only Finished prints. For starts 3 and 1, outputs are 3 then Finished, and 1,2,3 then Finished. Ask learners to write predictions before editing. A pre-test loop can have zero body executions; reaching the while line does not guarantee a pass.

6. Zero, one and several passes

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired investigation and role changes

Pairs run the same bounded loop with starts 4,3,1 after individual predictions. Driver enters the starting value in source, navigator checks the condition trace, then swap roles. Every learner records number of passes: 0,1,3. Support: circle the start and update. Stretch: choose a new upper limit and design zero/one/several-pass tests without adding input validation.

7. What would stop this repetition?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paper debugging and all-student check

Discuss without executing an unbounded loop. If count starts at 1 and while count <= 3 has no update, printing count never changes the condition. It remains True. Expected repair: count = count + 1 inside the body. Model the school editor Stop control before learners experiment, then run only the corrected bounded version. Recheck termination by tracing count=4.

8. Exit ticket: the stopping check

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit ticket

For count=1, while count < 3 prints and increments, output is 1 and 2. Last update makes count 3, then condition False. Start at 3 gives zero passes. Ask for the final failed condition check rather than only the printed sequence. Use errors to revisit < versus <= next lesson.
